findings.finding: unread_reply_warning is skipped whenever payload_file is set, but adapter none never reads the payload; --payload-file without --from records findings_count 0 with no warning.
findings.suggestion: Warn whenever adapter is none on a completed spec/code/doubt row; sharper message when a payload was ignored; add test.

findings.finding: Later-report-wins can undercount after a partial retry (fail-closed); docstring does not say so.
findings.suggestion: Document it and pin with a test.

findings.finding: Docstring claims Playwright ids are one result per test, but the reader folds projects into one id; multi-project runs undercount (fail-closed).
Test gaps: whole-suite path, retry= replacement, non-empty base, mixed JUnit+Playwright.
Stray empty comment; the two tests parse output differently.
read_junit_cases test does not check agreement with read_junit on classname fallback and base.

Claim under doubt: the surface check never credits more cases than really passed — read_junit_cases counts raw testcase rows per folded id; two identical passing rows inside one report (a concatenated junit-NN.xml) count as 2, so tests_run equal to twice the real count would pass F11. Across reports counts replace, not sum.
findings.suggestion: Count distinct (classname, raw name) per id and pin with a duplicate-row test.

findings.finding: The warning only fires when `adapter == "none"`. A row recorded with `--from code-reviewer` but a missing/mis-parsed payload is not warned unless `build_review_evidence` hard-errors on that shape — if it can return 0 findings for a native adapter with no payload, the spec's "warn when a completed row is recorded without its reviewer reply" is only partially implemented (exactly the failure mode the smoke campaign hit: the runner did pass `--from`, the reply just wasn't read). The diff itself can't show whether that path raises; if it doesn't, this is a live gap.
findings.suggestion: Warn whenever a completed spec/code/doubt row ends with `findings_count == 0` and no reply text was actually parsed, regardless of adapter; or verify and pin with a test that `--from code-reviewer` without a readable payload cannot silently record 0.

findings.finding: The distinct-case key is `(classname, name)`, but the id also folds on the `file` attribute. Two rows for the same test — one carrying `file` (empty/absent classname) and one carrying `classname` (fallback path) — produce different keys and count 2 for one real case. In a concatenated multi-report junit-NN.xml (the exact scenario the doubt finding called out), this is a fail-open overcount: `tests_run` equal to the inflated count would pass F11. The duplicate-row test only covers identical rows and same-attr rows.
findings.suggestion: Key distinctness on a normalized identity consistent with id folding (e.g. `(resolved file path, name)` rather than raw `(classname, name)`), and add a mixed file/classname duplicate test.

findings.finding: Test 1 uses `json.loads(out)` directly while tests 2–3 use `raw_decode(out[out.index("{"):])` with a comment saying run_tool merges stderr into stdout. If that's true, test 1 is the broken one (it would raise on any stderr noise); if false, the inconsistency is harmless but the reason is unverified. Either way, one of the three tests encodes a wrong assumption about the harness.
findings.suggestion: Parse identically in all three tests, using whichever form matches the harness's actual output contract.

findings.finding: An unreadable/unparseable staged report is skipped entirely and previously-known counts from an earlier report for the same ids are kept — but a parseable but partial report replaces them. This is documented fail-closed, so not a bug per se, but the interaction with `counts.update` also means a report that parses but is truncated mid-stream (ET succeeds on well-formed prefix? no — ParseError returns {}) is fine; the only real residual risk is the mixed-attr overcount above. No action needed beyond the item above.  Everything else checks out: the recorder stays at spec'd size with the helper in `lib`, the campaign doc names `--from`/`--payload-file`, no smoke exemption code was added, the F11 check now compares in the runner's case unit via `read_junit_cases` while keeping the fail-closed `cases < tests_run` refusal, and the three new surface tests cover accepted-count, overstated-count, failing-case, whole-suite, and partial-retry paths — these are behavioral, not just call-through.  Overall: ship-with-fixes — the mixed-attribute overcount is a genuine fail-open hole in an otherwise deliberately fail-closed gate, and the warning condition should be tightened or proven complete.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
